correctness.rationale: Symmetrization preserves the objective and pairwise-uniform marginals; each occupancy orbit has a two-coordinate law determined only by its collision count; the mean-collision condition is both necessary and sufficient after symmetrization. The endpoint mixtures then give exact sharp all-distinct bounds, and exact finite enumeration verifies the constructions for small alphabets.

originality.rationale: The inspected hashing, orthogonal-array, finite-exchangeability, and probability-bounds literature did not reveal the exact one-moment reduction for all occupancy-invariant objectives or the resulting arbitrary-q all-distinct interval. Closest sources establish pair-collision expectations, construct pairwise-independent/orthogonal-array families, or solve different event-independence extremal problems.

value.rationale: The result converts an entire class of high-dimensional extremal problems under pairwise independence into a one-dimensional moment problem, yields two-occupancy extremizers, and makes the standard collision-free first-moment guarantee exactly sharp while adding a sharp opposite bound.
